{
"Design Pattern": "A reusable, general solution to a commonly occurring problem within a given context in software design, serving as a template that can be applied across different situations.",
"Factory Pattern": "A creational design pattern that abstracts and encapsulates the process of object creation, allowing clients to instantiate objects without specifying their concrete classes.",
"Observer Pattern": "A behavioral design pattern that defines a one-to-many dependency between objects, enabling loose coupling by allowing observers to be notified automatically when a subject's state changes.",
"Strategy Pattern": "A behavioral design pattern that defines a family of interchangeable algorithms, encapsulating each one and allowing the behavior of an object to vary at runtime.",
"Singleton Pattern": "A creational design pattern that restricts the instantiation of a class to a single instance and provides a global point of access to that instance.",
"Creational Pattern": "A category of design patterns that focuses on mechanisms for object creation, abstracting the instantiation process to make systems independent of how their objects are created and composed.",
"Structural Pattern": "A category of design patterns that deals with object composition, defining ways to assemble objects and classes into larger structures while keeping them flexible and efficient.",
"Behavioral Pattern": "A category of design patterns that focuses on communication and the assignment of responsibilities between objects, defining how they interact and collaborate.",
"Object Creation": "The process of instantiating new objects in a software system, including allocating memory and initializing their state.",
"Object Composition": "A design principle in which complex objects are built by combining simpler objects, promoting flexibility and code reuse over inheritance.",
"Loose Coupling": "A design principle in which components or objects have minimal dependencies on one another, allowing them to be modified, replaced, or reused independently.",
"Instantiation": "The act of creating a concrete instance of a class, allocating memory for the object and initializing its properties.",
"Runtime Behavior": "The actions and interactions exhibited by a software system during its execution, as opposed to behavior defined at compile time.",
"Software Design Problem": "A recurring challenge or issue encountered during the design of software systems that requires a structured and reusable approach to solve.",
"Reusable Solution": "A generalized approach or template that can be applied to multiple problems or contexts, reducing redundancy and promoting consistency across software designs."
}
